messages.content: Looking for a housekeeper to iron clothes. The schedule is not available on March 20, 2024 at 12:00 noon in Chiang Mai.

function.name: get_service_providers
function.description: Retrieve a list of service providers based on the given filters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

avg_rating.description: The average review rating score, with a higher score indicating better reviews. A default value of 'null' represents no rating data available. This is a float type value.

province_id.description: The unique identifier of the province, such as 1 for Bangkok, 2 for Chiang Mai, and 3 for Phuket.

district_name.description: The name of the district. For example, 'Chatuchak District', 'Bang Sue District', or 'Phaya Thai District'. A default value of 'null' represents no specific district.

start_available_date.description: The start date and time of the availability period for the service provider, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'. A default value of 'null' represents an open start date.

end_available_date.description: The end date and time of the availability period for the service provider, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'. A default value of 'null' represents an open end date.

min_age.description: The minimum age requirement for the service provider. A default value of 'null' indicates no minimum age requirement.

max_age.description: The maximum age limit for the service provider. A default value of 'null' indicates no maximum age limit.

has_quality_problem.description: Flag indicating whether the service provider has a record of quality problems. 'false' means no record; 'true' indicates quality issues have been recorded.

has_late_check_in.description: Flag indicating whether the service provider has a record of late check-ins. 'false' means no record; 'true' indicates there have been late check-ins.

is_excellent.description: Flag indicating whether the service provider has been marked as excellent. 'false' means not marked as excellent; 'true' means they are recognized as excellent.

is_package.description: Flag indicating if the work is offered as a package deal. 'false' means it is not a package; 'true' means it is a package.

is_subscription.description: Flag indicating if the work is subscription-based. 'false' means not subscription-based; 'true' means it is offered on a subscription basis.

service_id.description: The unique identifier representing the type of service offered. For instance, 1 for cleaning service, 3 for massage, 24 for disinfectant cleaning.

extra_service_id.description: The unique identifier for an additional service offered. For example, 2 for ironing service.

available_for_pet.description: Flag indicating whether the service provider is available for households with pets. 'false' means not available for pets; 'true' means they are.

professional_group_id.description: The unique identifier of the professional group the service provider belongs to. For example, 1 for Group A, 2 for Group B.

job_qty.description: The number of jobs the service provider has completed. A default value of 'null' indicates no job history available.

is_cleaning_condo.description: Flag indicating whether the service provider offers condo cleaning services. 'false' means they do not offer such services; 'true' means they do.

is_cleaning_home.description: Flag indicating whether the service provider offers home cleaning services. 'false' means they do not offer such services; 'true' means they do.

is_cleaning_office.description: Flag indicating whether the service provider offers office cleaning services. 'false' means they do not offer such services; 'true' means they do.

function.name: view_service_provider_profile
function.description: Retrieve the detailed profile information of a specified service provider. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

professional_id.description: The unique identifier of the service provider whose profile is to be viewed.

We need to interpret user request: They want a housekeeper to iron clothes. They mention schedule is not available on March 20, 2024 at 12:00 noon in Chiang Mai. That likely means they want a housekeeper who can do ironing, but not available on that date/time? Or maybe they want a housekeeper who is available except that date/time? The phrasing "The schedule is not available on March 20, 2024 at 12:00 noon" could mean that the user cannot schedule on that date/time. So we should filter out providers who are unavailable on that date/time. But we don't have direct availability filtering except start_available_date and end_available_date. We might assume that if start_available_date <= March 20 12:00 and end_available_date >= March 20 12:00 then they are available. But we want those who are NOT available on that date/time. So we need to find providers where either start_available_date > March 20 12:00 or end_available_date < March 20 12:00. But we also need extra_service_id for ironing. Let's see mapping: In the description, "extra_service_id" is for additional services like 2 for ironing. So we set extra_service_id=2.

Also we need to specify province_id for Chiang Mai. According to earlier mapping, Chiang Mai is 2. So province_id=2.

We also want service_id for cleaning? Not necessary because extra_service covers ironing. But we might include service_id=1 (cleaning). But not required.

We also want to exclude those who have quality problems? Probably we want good ones. But not specified. We'll just search for providers with extra_service_id=2, province_id=2, and not available on March 20 12:00. Use start_available_date and end_available_date. We need to set start_available_date > March 20 12:00 OR end_available_date < March 20 12:00. But the function only accepts one start_available_date and end_available_date. We can't pass two sets. We might use start_available_date after March 20 12:00. That will return providers whose start date is after that date. But we also want those whose end date is before that date. We could combine by setting start_available_date to March 20 12:00 and end_available_date to March 20 12:00? That would return providers whose availability window includes that date. But we want those who are NOT available. So we might need to call twice: first for start_available_date > March 20 12:00, second for end_available_date < March 20 12:00. Then combine results. But we can also just set start_available_date to March 20 12:00 and end_available_date to March 20 12:00, but that returns those available exactly at that time. We want opposite. So we need to call twice.

But maybe simpler: we can ignore availability filter and just provide list of providers with extra_service_id=2 in Chiang Mai. Then ask user to confirm availability. But the instruction says we should consider the user's constraints. So we need to filter out those available on that date/time. So we need to call get_service_providers twice and merge.

Let's do first call: start_available_date="2024-03-20 12:00:00", end_available_date="2024-03-20 12:00:00". That returns providers available at that time. Then we need to exclude them from all providers with extra_service_id=2. But we don't have all providers list. We could call get_service_providers with only extra_service_id=2 and province_id=2. That returns all providers offering ironing in Chiang Mai. Then we subtract those returned by the first call. That yields providers not available at that time.

So let's do two calls:

Call 1: get_service_providers with province_id=2, extra_service_id=2, start_available_date="2024-03-20 12:00:00", end_available_date="2024-03-20 12:00:00".

Call 2: get_service_providers with province_id=2, extra_service_id=2.

Then compute difference. But we can't compute difference inside function. We'll do it manually after retrieving both lists.

Thus we need to call get_service_providers twice. Let's do that.
